destination.name: Royal National Park
destination.tagline: Sydney's southern national park, with surf beaches, a coastal walk and clifftop rocks an hour from the CBD.
destination.description: Royal National Park covers about 16,000 ha south of Sydney and was proclaimed in April 1879, making it the world's second-oldest national park after Yellowstone. Its coast has surf beaches and the 27 km Bundeena to Otford Coast Track, with Wattamolla's lagoon and waterfall, Wedding Cake Rock and the Figure Eight Pools as the best-known stops. The Hacking River runs through the park at Audley, where an 1893 boatshed hires canoes and rowboats. The park was renamed Royal National Park in 1955 after the 1954 tour by Queen Elizabeth II.
whyVisit: Walk the Bundeena to Otford Coast Track

goodToKnow.title: Arrive early in summer
goodToKnow.detail: Rangers close the Wattamolla access road once the car park fills; on summer weekends and public holidays aim to be parked by about 9:30 AM.

goodToKnow.title: Vehicle fee
goodToKnow.detail: Entry is $12 per vehicle per day, but you do not pay if you only drive through without stopping; the park is open 7 AM to 8:30 PM.

goodToKnow.title: Figure Eight Pools tides
goodToKnow.detail: The Figure Eight Pools at Burning Palms Beach are safe only at low tide, and Wedding Cake Rock is viewed from behind a safety fence and closed in total fire bans.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} give cool, clear walking weather on the Coast Track and avoid the summer weekends when the park may reach capacity and close roads.
